claims.title: Compile sharp late-task precision under a supplied symmetric source contract, with native transfer and future-information limits

quoted_fields.interface: A fixed finite real symmetric source, the actual whole norm-ball prior, late symmetric task T, freely selectable unit real inputs and the declared per-call worst-case error contract. Exact-interval and native nonlinear/scalar transfers each require their separately supplied geometry, smoothness, detector and error interfaces; they are not inferred from finite source records.
quoted_fields.failure: N997's general operator/history and fixed-menu results remain valid and distinct; N996's vector/transpose grammar is not imported. Restricted/rational-only inputs, extra source structure, additional joint noise restrictions or noncentral history can change the sharp value. Outer noisy posteriors do not inherit the full-family lower bound. Nonlinear reduction is sound, not globally minimax over all native nonlinear procedures. A C5 strongly convex bump defeats unguarded derivative transfer from finite gradient data. Programmable scalar readout is an actual additional native interface, not free compression of a previously measured vector. Same-information optimal-recovery/retaining procedures tie; no device, physical calibration, lifetime advantage or historical priority is established.
